title: Stance Openers & the Rhythm of a Live Interview

sections.content: You know stance adverbs like *francamente*, *sinceramente* and *lamentablemente* from B2 Unit 1. In a live interview, speakers combine those single-word adverbs with conversational stance phrases that open a candid answer or pivot to a conclusion: *a decir verdad* ('to tell the truth'), *para ser sincero / sincera* ('to be honest' — agrees in gender with the speaker), *con franqueza* ('frankly'), *la verdad* ('honestly'), *en todo caso* ('in any case') and *dicho esto* ('that said'). Like B2's stance adverbs, they sit outside the main clause and are set off by a comma in writing and a brief pause in speech.

sections.title: Spoken stance openers in interviews
rows: Opens a candid admission (*A decir verdad, al principio dudaba.*).
Agrees with the speaker's gender (*Para ser sincera, madrugar cuesta.*).
Signals a direct, unvarnished view (*Con franqueza, la clientela manda.*).
Pivots to a balanced conclusion (*Dicho esto, no cambiaría de oficio.*).

items.spanish: A decir verdad, abrir la panadería fue más difícil de lo que imaginaba.
items.english: To tell the truth, opening the bakery was harder than I imagined.

items.spanish: Para ser sincera, los primeros meses casi no dormía por el ritmo del horno.
items.english: To be honest, the first few months I barely slept because of the pace of the oven.

items.spanish: Con franqueza, la clientela del barrio nos sostuvo desde el primer día.
items.english: Frankly, the neighbourhood clientele supported us from day one.

items.spanish: Dicho esto, volvería a elegir este trabajo sin dudarlo.
items.english: That said, I would choose this work again without hesitating.

sections.content: Remember gender agreement in *para ser sincero* (male speaker) vs *para ser sincera* (female speaker), and don't stack two stance openers back to back (*Francamente, a decir verdad…* sounds heavy — pick one per turn).
